children: The 100-key hotel will be developed in two phases, strengthening IHCL’s presence in the state’s leisure market

Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) has signed a SeleQtions hotel in Athirapilly, Kerala, as a conversion and expansion project. The 100-key hotel will be developed in two phases, strengthening IHCL’s presence in the state’s leisure market.

The first phase will comprise 37 existing operational keys, with the remaining inventory to be added as part of the expansion. The hotel will feature an all-day dining restaurant, a wine and beer lounge and a rooftop dining experience. Facilities for meetings and social gatherings will include banquet venues and meeting rooms, while recreational offerings will comprise a swimming pool, fitness centre and spa with multiple treatment rooms.

Suma Venkatesh, Executive Vice President - Real Estate & Development, IHCL, said, “Kerala continues to be a key leisure market with its diverse tourism offerings and strong connectivity. Athirapilly, with its proximity to the iconic Athirapilly Falls and easy access from Kochi, presents an attractive opportunity to further strengthen our presence in the state. The signing is in line with our focus on expanding our portfolio across distinctive leisure destinations. We are delighted to partner with the Kshema Group for this project and bring the SeleQtions experience to Athirapilly.”

Located in Thrissur district on the banks of the Chalakudy River, the hotel is adjacent to Athirapilly Falls, Kerala’s largest waterfall. It is also in proximity to Cochin International Airport and forms part of leisure itineraries connecting Kochi and Munnar.

Abhinand Basant, Director, Kshema Group, said, “We are delighted to partner with IHCL to bring the SeleQtions brand to Athirappilly. This partnership is an important milestone in our hospitality journey and reflects our commitment to developing distinctive destinations that are deeply connected to their location and surroundings. We look forward to working closely with IHCL to create a memorable hospitality experience in Athirappilly and contribute to the region’s growing tourism potential.”
